Hi, I'm Ifechukwu.

I'm a data analyst who likes the part of the job where something looks wrong in the numbers and nobody knows why yet. I trace it to its source, fix the data, and build the report that makes the answer obvious.

My work has covered research data, restaurant sales, business datasets of 100,000+ rows and hospital medication records. In each one I did the same three things: found the problem, picked the right tool, and measured what changed. At Mega Harvest Research Institute I cleaned multi-source research data and cut executive reporting time by 30%. At Excelerate I built Power BI dashboards that cut the time stakeholders spent interpreting data by 35%.

I trained as a pharmacist at the University of Lagos, which taught me to check every number twice before someone acts on it. I'm Microsoft PL-300 certified and I hold the Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate.

Experience

Four roles, newest first. What I noticed, what I did, and what changed.

Oct 2026 to nowPart time

Research Data Associate

Mega Harvest Research Institute

Research reports were slow because data was tracked by hand and records were kept differently in every department. I built standardized cleaning and validation workflows across multi-source datasets that removed duplicate records and discrepancies, and I turned raw survey and operational data into structured summaries. Executive reporting turnaround dropped by 30%.

I also lead the Novelty stream. I review research topics across academic databases and complete Excel novelty maps that show how much of each topic is already covered, so the team avoids repeating work. I direct a team of volunteer analysts: I assign topics, give instructions, review what they submit and grade their performance.

Sep 2026 to Nov 2026Internship project

Data Analyst Intern

Team Oreo

A restaurant's sales data gave no clear view of what drove revenue or where money leaked. I cleaned and imported 1,795 of 1,800 records into MySQL and wrote SQL to calculate revenue, average order value, best and worst sellers, waste percentage, sales by day, and peak hours and channel. I cross checked the team's Excel KPIs against my SQL results so everyone could trust the numbers.

I then compared discounted and full price orders on order value, quantity and customer rating to show whether discounts were growing revenue or only giving it away, and presented to the team how each proposed solution would fix the problems the data revealed.

Mar 2026 to Aug 2026Internship, remote

Data Analyst Intern

Excelerate

Business datasets of 100,000+ rows had inconsistent reporting standards and quality problems that put every downstream analysis at risk. I built Power Query pipelines to clean and normalize the data, wrote 10+ SQL queries across two relational datasets, and ran exploratory analysis to find the metrics that mattered.

  • Designed and deployed 4 interactive Power BI dashboards for 5 stakeholders, cutting the time they spent interpreting data by 35%.
  • Delivered visualizations for a 13 person cross functional team working across time zones.
  • Analyzed a 7,543 record university applicant dataset and a learner engagement dataset where a Random Forest model reached 92% accuracy.
  • Wrote plain language executive reports and slide decks that non technical stakeholders could act on.
Aug 2025 to Nov 2025Internship

Pharmacy Intern and Intern Health Analyst

Sirona Hospital

Manual medication tracking was causing record errors and patient safety risks. I reviewed case notes and patient files and audited 50+ medication histories, which turned up 3 critical drug interactions and several gaps in therapy documentation that I corrected. I also compiled 15 structured therapy outcome reports that gave the healthcare team a clear, shared view of how patients were doing.
